contents.text:
The framework is MIT-licensed open source as of late November 2026, so I don't need to pay for the framework itself. Hosted, configured agents for businesses are sold through louis-agent.dev, and the roadmap puts the first sale after Phase 9, which hasn't happened yet. I don't know the prices, so I'll leave those out.

I'm weighing whether the README's documentation path should close the answer, and whether I should open a page or just offer follow-up options like "How do I use it in my company?" I'll lead with the answer, avoid lists, and note that the docs give no price for a hosted agent, only a planned monthly fee plus usage that isn't set yet.

The framework itself costs nothing to buy. It is open source under the MIT License, since 2026-11-25. Anyone may use, change and sell it, commercial use included, as long as the copyright notice and licence go with it.

Older releases keep their own licences. The 0.1.0 packages carry the PolyForm Noncommercial License, which does not allow commercial use.

I'm the framework's Orbi, and I sell nothing. The docs give no price for a hosted agent for a business. The roadmap says that offer is planned, with its first sale after Phase 9. For prices and buying, go to louis-agent.dev, the site that sells agents.

`README.md`

arguments.question: What would help most for your company?

choices.label: Use the framework free
choices.why: Read how to build an identity and a pack, then run it yourself.

choices.label: Check the MIT terms
choices.why: See the licence text and what it allows for commercial use.

choices.label: Ask about the hosted agent
choices.why: Where to go to buy one, at louis-agent.dev.
